messages:
marta: FYI, enterprise customer X seeing 401s + big tail latency after our midday policy update. They say requests are routed to eu-west but their key is bound to us-east.
ryan: Can you paste the example request + headers? any correlation ids? :eyes:
marta: From their support ticket: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXX' -H 'X-Client-Region: us-east' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
marta: They included this log excerpt: `req_id=ab12 x-region=eu-west routed_to=eu-west status=401 auth_err=key-region-mismatch` — looks like auth rejected after routing.
sophie: Uploading policy diff from the deployment earlier: we changed a failover block to allow weighted fallback instead of strict priority. In the UI the priority list got re-ordered by drag, looks reversed in deploy diff.
ryan: Oh — we had a bug where the deployed priority array was being interpreted LIFO, so primary became last entry. That would cause keys pinned to us-east to be routed to eu-west.
alex: Heads-up: billing saw a 3x egress bump from cross-region hops for that customer window — they opened a billing escalation.
marta: Customer reports the latency spiked to 800-1200ms for some requests when they hit eu-west (they're in us-east) — plus 401s on key checks.
customer-ops: We repro'd locally by creating a policy where priorities = ["eu-west", "us-east"] but UI showed "us-east" first. When the runtime evaluated it, it favored the first array element it saw (eu-west).
ryan: Repro steps I used:
```
# set policy
POST /v1/policies/123
{ "failover": { "priority": ["eu-west","us-east"], "weights": {"eu-west": 80, "us-east": 20}, "sticky": true } }
# send requests with key bound to us-east
for i in {1..50}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_east_key" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate; done
```
Observed ~75% traffic hitting eu-west and intermittent auth 401s.
sophie: The twist: weights were treated as relative integers but the UI label said percentages; also when sticky=true we were using a hashed affinity bucket keyed by policy position index. Since the priority array order flipped, sticky affinity pointed to the wrong region.
ryan: Quick mitigation: roll back the policy to previous commit (reverts priority order) and set sticky=false for the policy. Also clear the small session cache so requests re-evaluate routing.
marta: Customer runbook I sent: rotate the API key to a new one scoped to both regions (temporary) and confirm no 401s, then we'll reapply policy after fix.
alex: I've flagged billing for credit review; noted the cross-region egress spike in the ticket.
infra-bot: Deploy 2026-03-15T14:22:17Z rolled policy-update-priv-patch by @sophie (id: d9f3). Rollback available: d9f3 -> d8a2.
sophie: Root cause patch queued: fix priority array serialization order and make weights explicit percent vs absolute. Also adding a config validation: if sticky=true then error if priority ordering ambiguous.
ryan: Plan: revert now, run canary with 5% traffic, enable stricter policy validation, then reapply weights after verification.
marta: Customer notified of rollback and temporary key rotation. They want postmortem and credit estimate.
alex: I'll prepare credit calc and share by EOD.
customer-ops: thanks team — I'll keep ticket open until we confirm no further cross-region auths.
ryan: Follow-up action items:
- [ ] fix serializer bug (eng-runtime)
- [ ] add UI guard for reorder (devex)
- [ ] session cache clear endpoint for ops (eng-infra)
- [ ] billing credit estimate (finance)
- [ ] postmortem doc
marta: Great. Closing loop after rollback verification. :white_check_mark:
